subject: SLA tolerance waiver & monthly offset plan
messages:
From: Megan Holt <megan.holt@zephyrlabs.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Allan Pryce <allan@zephyrlabs.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: onboarding tolerance waiver + monthly offset plan

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — Zephyr's team is excited about the latency characteristics and the KV cache behavior you showed. We have one sticking point before legal will greenlight the pilot: the initial onboarding period will see large, bursty ingestion and a series of heavy nightly batch jobs for models training previews. That increases our risk of transient availability dips during month 0-3.

Could Redwood consider a temporary tolerance waiver to the standard uptime target and a corresponding monthly offset (service credit) schedule for the first 90 days? High level proposal from our side:
- Ramp uptime target: 30 days at 99.5%, next 60 days at 99.8% (after which standard 99.95% applies)
- If actual monthly uptime falls below the month-specific target, Zephyr receives a credit up to 12% of that month’s invoice (capped)
- We require measurement transparency (per-route uptime dashboard and raw incident logs) during the pilot

We'd prefer a short, signed amendment that pins this behavior to the onboarding period rather than changing the master SLA. Please let me know what Redwood can accept and any counterproposals.

Attachments: Zephyr-onboarding-runbook.docx (high-level batch schedule)

Best,
Megan

Megan —

Appreciate the clear ask and the runbook; this is exactly the sort of detail that helps us scope an exception. I'm looping in Legal and our Contracts lead (Laura) and Revenue Ops (Rishi) to review a pragmatic path. Draft SLA amendment attached — it preserves standard commitments after the 90-day onboarding and proposes a capped credit schedule, but we want to confirm caps and monitoring requirements with you.

Marked questions for Zephyr:
1) Can you share expected monthly spend during pilot so we can size the cap appropriately?
2) Are the nightly batch windows predictable (start/stop) or variable?
3) Do you need per-route (model-level) uptime or is tenancy-level sufficient?

I'm available for a quick call Thursday if helpful.

Best,
Markus Klein

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 08:46:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Request: onboarding tolerance waiver + monthly offset plan

Looping in suggested counterterms for discussion before we reply to Zephyr. Key goals: limit long-term exposure, require objective monitoring, and ensure operational levers (rate limits/ingestion throttles) are used before credits kick in. Proposed counter: 
- Temporary onboarding amendment (90 days max) with a phased uptime target: 30d at 99.6% (not 99.5), next 60d at 99.85%, then 99.95% standard
- Credit triggers only if on-call/ops runbook steps were followed (we require incident evidence and runbook sign-off)
- Credit cap: max 15% of monthly invoice in any onboarding month, and cumulative cap across 90 days equal to 25% of the total pilot spend
- Measurement: Redwood will provide per-tenant uptime + incident log extracts and an initial weekly sync for first 30 days
- If uptime shortfall persists beyond 90 days, escalation to VP Sales required for any extension

I attached a redlined amendment and an ops-runbook-template.xlsx we can ask Zephyr to complete and return.

If we agree internally, I'll have Legal prepare a DocuSign.

-Laura
Laura Bennett
Sr. Director, Contracts | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
Attachment: ops-runbook-template.xlsx
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Fwd: Request: onboarding tolerance waiver + monthly offset plan

Agree with Laura's lines. Two points from Revenue/Legal that should be explicit in the amendment:
1) A hard monthly absolute credit cap (not just percentage) tied to either $ value or a multiple of monthly MRR — suggest: max $45k per month during onboarding or 15% of monthly bill, whichever is lower. This prevents open-ended exposure if the pilot is large.
2) Require Zephyr to complete the ops-runbook template and commit to operational throttles (we can include predefined throttles) — credits will be withheld if throttles were not attempted.

I'll draft a short clause for the DocuSign: two signature blocks (Zephyr + Redwood) and a checkbox confirming runbook received. Also: any extension beyond 90 days needs VP Sales approval (no unilateral extensions).

Related: HubSpot deal link: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/8472 — please log updates.

-Rishi

Subject: Re: Request: onboarding tolerance waiver + monthly offset plan

Thanks — and thanks to your team for the fast turnaround. 

Zephyr is comfortable with the revised ramp (30d at 99.6%, 60d at 99.85%, then 99.95%), and the credit cap approach you proposed as long as the dollar cap is proportionate. Our expected monthly spend during the pilot is in the $60k-$80k range, so the $45k absolute cap looks reasonable as a safety valve. We will complete the ops-runbook-template.xlsx and sign the DocuSign amendment once you send it.

One operational ask: can Redwood expose per-model P95 latency metrics (24h) for the pilot so our ML team can monitor model-level regressions? That visibility will help us avoid hitting fallback strategies that could trigger credit windows.

Happy to hop on a 30-minute call Monday 10-10:30 PT to finalize language.

Best,
Megan
